checkpoints.description: Task 'tempo-reforge-fixes-v1' completed successfully.
[1/1] Preserve the all-time focus total for sessions that predate history, with a failing-first test

impact_assessment.why: Reforge stage 11 found that the analytics change sums an empty history to zero, so a pre-analytics session with completed_focus > 0 loses its all-time total.
impact_assessment.benefits: Upgraded session files keep a sensible total, and the backward-compatibility promise in ADR-007 is covered by a regression test.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: status payload total_focus_seconds keeps its meaning for history-bearing sessions; dependency: none; concurrency: snapshot stays read-only; state: only the empty-history fallback changes, no stored format.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Fall back to completed_focus * focus_seconds only when history is empty, add the failing-first test, and rerun the full gates before committing.

[1/2] Close the remaining reforge findings: canonical license links and a clock-rewind guard for a running timer

impact_assessment.why: Reforge stage 6 found the license points at local CLA/ACL paths that do not exist; stage 10 found a persisted monotonic clock that freezes a running timer after a reboot.
impact_assessment.benefits: The license text resolves to the canonical licensing repository, and a clock that moved backwards restarts the current run instead of stalling it; both get regression coverage.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: license prose and TempoApp's load path change; dependency: none; concurrency: the server stays single threaded; state: the guard rewrites started_at only when it is ahead of now, with no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the canonical upstream repository links, keep the AL-1.1 text otherwise intact, add a failing-first app test, run all gates, then audit the commit with reforge.

Task 'tempo-reforge-fixes-v3' completed successfully.
[1/1] Pause a stored running session on the first read in a new process, closing the persisted-monotonic-clock gap

impact_assessment.why: The session file persists a time.monotonic started_at, which is only meaningful within one boot; a restart can freeze the phase or make it jump through phases that never ran. The earlier rewind guard only covered the backwards case.
impact_assessment.benefits: A restart or reboot can no longer corrupt the timer or count downtime as focus; completed focus, history and the cycle count survive, and the policy is documented in ADR-008 and the README.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a running phase no longer resumes across a server restart; dependency: none; concurrency: the single-threaded server reads once per process; state: schema 1 is unchanged, but the first read writes the paused state.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pause on first read only (not every poll), add a failing-first restart test, document the policy, run all gates, and audit the commit with reforge.

Task 'tempo-reforge-fixes-v4' completed successfully.
[1/1] Close the connection after a POST to an unknown path so an unread body cannot desynchronise the next request

impact_assessment.why: A POST to /nope answers 404 without reading its body; on a keep-alive connection the leftover bytes are parsed as the next request, and the intermittent ConnectionAbortedError in the test suite came from that desync.
impact_assessment.benefits: The 404 path is deterministic, the test suite no longer flakes, and the HTTP handler closes every connection whose body it did not consume.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: POST 404 now carries Connection: close; dependency: none; concurrency: the single-threaded server is unchanged; state: no state change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a failing-first raw-socket test that asserts 404, Connection: close and EOF, then run the suite 30 times before committing.
